question: Why does vitamin C on a cut apple delay browning rather than simply slow it?
answer: Because it undoes the damage instead of stopping it. The apple's enzyme keeps turning phenols into quinones, which link up into brown pigment; vitamin C converts each quinone back and is used up doing so. While any remains the flesh stays pale; once it runs out, browning starts at full speed.
move: A shield that is used up by its work buys time, not safety.
ask: What protection in my life is quietly running out, giving me time but not safety?
source: Nicolas et al., Crit. Rev. Food Sci., 1994
reference: Nicolas, Richard-Forget, Goupy, Amiot & Aubert, Enzymatic browning reactions in apple and apple products, Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition 34, 109, 1994
